lessons.title: Explain and compare
lessons.subtitle: Week 9: AI for learning
lessons.body:
Comparing two explanations can reveal gaps in understanding. Check each explanation against a trusted learning source and your own reasoning.

Offline practice: Explain a familiar topic in plain language, then write a second explanation using a different example. Write your reasoning before looking at the quiz answers. Record one limitation or uncertainty. You can use paper or local notes; an online AI tool is optional.

Recap: explain yesterday’s key idea from memory, then check your notes. After a break, start with this recap and the first small step of today’s activity.

Complete all three quiz questions before moving on.
takeaways: Comparing two explanations can reveal gaps in understanding. Check each explanation against a trusted learning source and your own reasoning.
Apply the idea through the offline activity.
Keep reasoning, evidence, and limitations with your artifact.
lessons.sourceName: Google Machine Learning Crash Course — further reading

options: Share someone else’s private information to make the example realistic.

questions.prompt: You return to the “Explain and compare” lesson after a break without internet. What can you do next?
options: Assume a cloud assistant will respond without a connection.

questions.explanation: The lesson and practice do not require an online tool. Retrieval and a small saved activity help you resume.

lessons.title: Retrieval practice
lessons.subtitle: Week 9: AI for learning
lessons.body:
Retrieval practice means recalling information before checking notes. Remembering an answer is different from recognising it when it is visible.

Offline practice: Close this lesson and write three concepts from memory; reopen it and correct omissions. Write your reasoning before looking at the quiz answers. Record one limitation or uncertainty. You can use paper or local notes; an online AI tool is optional.

Recap: explain yesterday’s key idea from memory, then check your notes. After a break, start with this recap and the first small step of today’s activity.

Complete all three quiz questions before moving on.
takeaways: Retrieval practice means recalling information before checking notes. Remembering an answer is different from recognising it when it is visible.
Apply the idea through the offline activity.

lessons.title: Revision planning
lessons.subtitle: Week 9: AI for learning
lessons.body:
A realistic plan accounts for available time, prerequisites, and breaks. A plan should adapt when circumstances change rather than punish interruptions.

Offline practice: Create a fictional five-day plan and a shorter version for a busy week. Write your reasoning before looking at the quiz answers. Record one limitation or uncertainty. You can use paper or local notes; an online AI tool is optional.

Recap: explain yesterday’s key idea from memory, then check your notes. After a break, start with this recap and the first small step of today’s activity.

Complete all three quiz questions before moving on.
takeaways: A realistic plan accounts for available time, prerequisites, and breaks. A plan should adapt when circumstances change rather than punish interruptions.
Apply the idea through the offline activity.
Keep reasoning, evidence, and limitations with your artifact.

lessons.title: Resume after a break
lessons.subtitle: Week 9: AI for learning
lessons.body:
A recap helps identify what you remember and what needs refreshing. Resume with a manageable activity and preserve evidence of earlier work.

Offline practice: Create a return-after-a-break card with a recap question, a small task, and the next step. Write your reasoning before looking at the quiz answers. Record one limitation or uncertainty. You can use paper or local notes; an online AI tool is optional.

Recap: explain yesterday’s key idea from memory, then check your notes. After a break, start with this recap and the first small step of today’s activity.

Complete all three quiz questions before moving on.

Weekly completion task: save this week’s practice artifact. Confirm four steps: explain a key idea (recap); complete the practice activity (practice); record what you would verify and where (plan); show your artifact and explain one improvement (demonstrate).
takeaways: A recap helps identify what you remember and what needs refreshing. Resume with a manageable activity and preserve evidence of earlier work.
Apply the idea through the offline activity.
Keep reasoning, evidence, and limitations with your artifact.
